newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota to make official comment on chief's remarks.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to make official comment on chief's remarks.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Thursday it was preparing an official statement on comments by its president that the carmaker may shift its investment focus away from Britain if it stays out of Europe's single currency.
The remarks, made at a media reception in Tokyo on Wednesday night, set off a political row in Britain as it gears up for a general election campaign.

President Hiroshi Okuda said Toyota had no plan to scale back its current level of investment in Britain, but would favour putting new investment elsewhere in Europe if Britain chose to remain outside the European economic and monetary union (EMU).
The remarks plunged the ruling Conservative Party into fresh arguments over Europe and whether Britain should sign up for the first stage of monetary union in 1999.

"We're preparing an official company comment on the latest Reuters report," a senior Toyota official said on Thursday. He did not say when the announcement would be made, or give any details on its contents.
"Regardless of whether Britain joins (the EMU), I have a feeling that it would be excessive if we made additional (investments) in Britain," Okuda said on Wednesday evening.
Asked if Toyota's future strategy in Britain would change depending on whether Britain joined the EMU, he said: "It will change."
Asked if Toyota's investment would decrease if Britain opted out of the EMU, Okuda said: "Rather than decreasing the amount, we will leave investments as they are now.
"But if we were to make fresh investments, we would prefer to make them in continental Europe rather than Britain," he added.
Toyota last year built 117,000 cars at its plant in Derbyshire, central England. Britain is Toyota's only production base within the European Union.
Britain has to hold general elections by mid-1997, the end of parliament's five-year term.
